---
title: "A resolution tree for single-cell data"
---



In single-cell data the right number of clusters is rarely known in advance, so analysts look at several resolutions and keep the ones that hold up. This article builds that view with `emeans()`: it splits the cells in two, splits each half in two again, and so on, which gives a dendrogram whose depths are increasing resolutions. Reruns with other seeds show which branches are stable, and Seurat's Louvain clustering at matching cluster counts serves as an outside reference.

The data are GEO series [GSE233163](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE233163): about 73,000 mouse cells from two tissues (`scg` and `st`), at baseline and under obesity (Sarker et al., 2026). The authors distribute a Seurat object and a separate cell metadata table with their cell-type labels. Neither file ships with the package, and building the site does not re-run this article.


``` r
library(emeansR)
library(Seurat)
library(mclust)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(tidygraph)
library(ggraph)
```

## Setup



- Machine: Apple M2, 8 physical cores; R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24).
- Packages: emeansR 0.1.0, Seurat 6.0.0.
- `emeans()` runs on 7 threads.

The GEO file is gzipped twice, so `readRDS()` needs `gzcon()` to undo the inner layer. The object (Seurat 3.1 format, 8.7 GB in memory) has the authors' integrated expression but not their PCA or UMAP. The code below keeps only the integrated assay: 3,000 genes, 2,000 of them the variable features used for integration.


``` r
full <- readRDS(gzcon(gzfile(".dev/data/GSE233163_seurat_object.rds.gz", "rb")))
integrated <- full@assays$integrated
obj <- CreateSeuratObject(CreateAssay5Object(data = integrated@data), assay = "integrated")
VariableFeatures(obj) <- integrated@var.features
rm(full, integrated)
invisible(gc())
obj
#> An object of class Seurat 
#> 3000 features across 73042 samples within 1 assay 
#> Active assay: integrated (3000 features, 2000 variable features)
#>  1 layer present: data

meta <- read.csv(".dev/data/GSE233163_cells_metadata.csv.gz")
cell_type <- meta$cell_type[match(colnames(obj), meta$id)]
table(cell_type, useNA = "ifany")
#> cell_type
#>                dendritic            endothelial_1            endothelial_2 
#>                     1707                     4296                     2260 
#>            endothelial_3               macrophage              microglia_1 
#>                     1175                     5886                      470 
#>                   neuron                 pericyte           schwann_cell_1 
#>                      406                     1501                    47772 
#>           schwann_cell_2 schwann_cell_myelinating         t_reg_lymphocyte 
#>                     2308                     3991                     1270
```

PCA and UMAP use the settings recorded in the object's command log: 30 components, then UMAP on the first 20 with cosine distance, 30 neighbours and `min.dist = 0.3`. Clustering runs on the same 20 components.


``` r
embedding <- local({
  obj <- ScaleData(obj, verbose = FALSE)
  obj <- RunPCA(obj, npcs = 30, seed.use = 12345, verbose = FALSE)
  obj <- RunUMAP(obj, dims = 1:20, n.neighbors = 30, metric = "cosine", min.dist = 0.3,
                 seed.use = 12345, verbose = FALSE)
  list(pcs = Embeddings(obj, "pca")[, 1:20], umap = Embeddings(obj, "umap"))
})
```


``` r
pcs <- embedding$pcs
umap <- embedding$umap
rm(obj)
invisible(gc())
dim(pcs)
#> [1] 73042    20
```

## Recursive bisection

`bisect_tree()` keeps one label per cell and depth. At each depth, `emeans()` splits every node with at least `min_cells` cells in two, using only that node's cells; smaller nodes keep their label. A label is the path from the root, so `"1.2.1"` is the first child of the second child of the root.


``` r
bisect_tree <- function(x, max_depth = 5, min_cells = 200, seed = 1) {
  labels <- matrix("1", nrow(x), max_depth + 1, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("level_", 0:max_depth)))
  for (depth in seq_len(max_depth)) {
    parent <- labels[, depth]
    child <- parent
    nodes <- unique(parent)
    for (i in seq_along(nodes)) {
      idx <- which(parent == nodes[i])
      if (length(idx) < min_cells) next
      fit <- emeans(x[idx, , drop = FALSE], 2, nepochs = 3, seed = seed * 1000 + depth * 100 + i)
      child[idx] <- paste0(nodes[i], ".", fit$cluster)
    }
    labels[, depth + 1] <- child
  }
  labels
}

max_depth <- 5
tree_time <- system.time(tree <- bisect_tree(pcs, max_depth))[["elapsed"]]
levels <- 1:max_depth
n_clusters <- map_int(levels, ~ n_distinct(tree[, .x + 1]))
tibble(level = levels, clusters = n_clusters)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   level clusters
#>   <int>    <int>
#> 1     1        2
#> 2     2        4
#> 3     3        8
#> 4     4       16
#> 5     5       31
```

## Stability across seeds

The tree is rebuilt with ten more seeds. Cluster names are arbitrary, so the comparison uses measures that ignore labels: the adjusted Rand index (ARI) per level, and for each cell the Jaccard overlap between its cluster in the reference tree and its cluster in the rerun.


``` r
reruns <- map(2:11, ~ bisect_tree(pcs, max_depth, seed = .x))
```


``` r
cell_jaccard <- function(a, b) {
  tab <- table(a, b)
  jac <- tab / (outer(rowSums(tab), colSums(tab), "+") - tab)
  jac[cbind(match(a, rownames(tab)), match(b, colnames(tab)))]
}

seed_ari <- map_dfr(seq_along(reruns), function(r) {
  tibble(run = r, level = levels,
         ari = map_dbl(levels, ~ adjustedRandIndex(tree[, .x + 1], reruns[[r]][, .x + 1])))
})

stability <- map(levels, function(l) {
  rowMeans(sapply(reruns, function(run) cell_jaccard(tree[, l + 1], run[, l + 1])))
})
```

## Louvain at matching resolutions

Seurat's `FindClusters()` runs over a range of resolutions on a shared nearest neighbour graph of the same 20 components (`k.param = 20`, as the authors used). Each tree level is paired with the resolution whose cluster count is closest to its own.


``` r
resolutions <- c(0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2)
louvain_time <- system.time({
  graphs <- FindNeighbors(pcs, k.param = 20, verbose = FALSE)
  louvain <- FindClusters(graphs$snn, resolution = resolutions, verbose = FALSE)
})[["elapsed"]]
```


``` r
louvain_k <- map_int(louvain, n_distinct)
match_res <- map_int(n_clusters, ~ which.min(abs(louvain_k - .x)))

agreement <- tibble(
  level = levels,
  clusters = n_clusters,
  resolution = resolutions[match_res],
  louvain_clusters = louvain_k[match_res],
  ari_louvain = map2_dbl(levels, match_res, ~ adjustedRandIndex(tree[, .x + 1], louvain[[.y]])),
  ari_cell_type = map_dbl(levels, ~ adjustedRandIndex(tree[, .x + 1], cell_type))
)
agreement
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   level clusters resolution louvain_clusters ari_louvain ari_cell_type
#>   <int>    <int>      <dbl>            <int>       <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1     1        2      0.001                3       0.163         0.175
#> 2     2        4      0.001                3       0.533         0.517
#> 3     3        8      0.01                 8       0.937         0.846
#> 4     4       16      0.2                 16       0.541         0.741
#> 5     5       31      1                   33       0.181         0.590
```

Louvain returns at least 3 clusters even at resolution 0.001, so levels 1 and 2 are compared with that coarsest Louvain partition.

One e-means tree takes 0.2 seconds. Building the neighbour graph and running Louvain at 14 resolutions takes 288.6 seconds.

## The tree

Node size is the number of cells; colour is the mean seed stability of the node's cells at its depth.


``` r
node_stability <- map_dfr(levels, function(l) {
  tibble(name = tree[, l + 1], stability = stability[[l]]) |>
    group_by(name) |>
    summarise(stability = mean(stability), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(depth = l)
})

# A node that stops splitting keeps its name at deeper levels; keep its first depth.
nodes <- map_dfr(0:max_depth, ~ count(tibble(name = tree[, .x + 1]), name, name = "cells") |> mutate(depth = .x)) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  slice_min(depth) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(node_stability, by = c("name", "depth"))

edges <- nodes |>
  filter(depth > 0) |>
  transmute(from = sub("\\.[^.]+$", "", name), to = name)

graph <- tbl_graph(nodes = nodes, edges = edges)
ggraph(graph, layout = "dendrogram", height = -depth) +
  geom_edge_elbow(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = cells, colour = stability)) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey40") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8) +
  labs(colour = "seed\nstability", size = "cells") +
  theme_void()
```

## Clusters on the UMAP

Each panel is one level and shows a random 20,000 cells.


``` r
set.seed(1)
show <- sample(nrow(umap), min(20000, nrow(umap)))
cells <- map_dfr(levels, function(l) {
  tibble(umap_1 = umap[show, 1], umap_2 = umap[show, 2],
         level = sprintf("level %d: %d clusters", l, n_clusters[l]),
         cluster = tree[show, l + 1], stability = stability[[l]][show])
})
```


``` r
ggplot(cells, aes(umap_1, umap_2, colour = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.1) +
  facet_wrap(~level) +
  guides(colour = "none") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
```

![plot of chunk umap-clusters](single-cell-figs/umap-clusters-1.png)


``` r
ggplot(cells, aes(umap_1, umap_2, colour = stability)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.1) +
  facet_wrap(~level) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(colour = "seed\nstability") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Stability against resolution


``` r
seed_summary <- seed_ari |>
  group_by(level) |>
  summarise(median = median(ari), low = min(ari), high = max(ari), .groups = "drop")

bind_rows(
  seed_summary |> transmute(level, ari = median, low, high, comparison = "e-means, other seeds"),
  agreement |> transmute(level, ari = ari_louvain, comparison = "Louvain, matched resolution"),
  agreement |> transmute(level, ari = ari_cell_type, comparison = "author cell types")
) |>
  left_join(tibble(level = levels, clusters = n_clusters), by = "level") |>
  ggplot(aes(clusters, ari, colour = comparison)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high, group = comparison), data = \(d) filter(d, !is.na(low)),
              fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = n_clusters) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "clusters (log scale)", y = "adjusted Rand index", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
